findings.problem: API-PTY-019 ('Creation is allowed under WARN too') and ADR-PTY-028 contradict three upstream statements. REQ-PTY-091 reads 'While the credit-overrun action is BLOCK_WITH_OVERRIDE, when a user requests approval…'. ADR-PTY-016 says 'A request is accepted only under BLOCK_WITH_OVERRIDE'. REQ-PTY-088 says that under WARN no request is needed. The silent path (a request created under WARN) has no rule, no catalog code and no test case.
findings.fix: Follow the upstream. Add RULE-PTY-035 'Request only under BLOCK_WITH_OVERRIDE' with catalog row PTY-422-OVERRIDE-NOT-REQUIRED. Raise it in API-PTY-019 after the server-side check and add it to the api-spec 422 codes. Add an AC (WARN, OVER_LIMIT → refused) and a backend TC. Remove the WARN sentence from API-PTY-019 and ADR-PTY-028 through a new ADR that revises ADR-PTY-028.

findings.problem: The plan says its given-usage table 'cites the SRS A9 rows and adds none', but it diverges from the current A9 in four places. (1) It lists modules.tenant as `TenantContext` and its listeners use `TenantContext.runAs`, while A9 now names `TenantRunner`. Checklist C4 does permit runAs; the defect is the drift from upstream. (2) It lists modules.module as `META-INF/erp/modules/pty.yaml` instead of `docs/api-docs/module/index.md`. (3) It keeps the modules.common row and says '15 uses', while A9 has 14 rows. (4) ADR-PTY-044 is missing from the Decisions table, and registry-exec-be says 'Next free ADR: ADR-PTY-044' although ADR-PTY-044 exists. Separately, backend test-plan note N7 still cites the withdrawn ADR-PTY-025 exemption.
findings.fix: Align the plan's given-usage table to A9 (14 rows, TenantRunner, the module api doc; no common row) and change the CORE listener text to TenantRunner. Add ADR-PTY-044 to Decisions and set next free ADR to ADR-PTY-045 in registry-exec-be. Change N7 to ADR-PTY-039.

findings.clause: "The module serves only its own lookup keys through `OwnedLookups.read(...)`" (checklist C6)
findings.problem: PTY owns five lookup keys, seeded with OWNER_MODULE_CODE 'PTY'. The plan states no `OwnedLookups.read(...)` use. The frontend's lookup reads (F2 LOOKUP hooks) therefore have no stated serving mechanism on the owner side.
findings.fix: In CORE (Lookups), state that PTY serves CUSTOMER_GROUP, ADDRESS_TYPE, CREDIT_OVERRUN_ACTION, CREDIT_CHECK_RESULT and CREDIT_OVERRIDE_STATUS through `OwnedLookups.read(...)` with owner PTY. Validation keeps `MdlLookupApi.readActiveValuesByKey` (C5). Add the given-usage row in SRS A9 and contract Part 4 if `OwnedLookups` is a published seam of modules.mdl or modules.common; otherwise record the reason in an ADR.

findings.problem: `CustomerQueryService.globalSearch` (API-PTY-027) carries `isAuthenticated()` and checks VIEW in code. ADR-PTY-039 §3 accepts this as an exception, but the checklist line allows none.
findings.fix: Keep REQ-PTY-043 behaviour (an empty list, not a 403) at the entry layer. The controller and the `PtyPartyApi.globalSearchCustomers` delegate each test PERM_PTY_CUSTOMER_VIEW through `SecurityContextHelper` and return an empty list without it. Otherwise they call a service method annotated `hasAuthority(T(…PtyPermissions).PERM_PTY_CUSTOMER_VIEW)`. Revise ADR-PTY-039 §3 and SEC-BE to remove the exception.

findings.clause: P1 — a stated guard with no test case (N13 claims 9/9)
findings.problem: Four guards the plan states have no barrier-synchronised TC. (a) API-PTY-004 versus API-PTY-019, serialised by the Customer lock. (b) API-PTY-004 versus an approval or a use (QR-PTY-039 plus compare-and-set, with three spelled-out outcomes). (c) The guest email race in API-PTY-034 (REQUIRES_NEW plus one re-match); TC-PTY-172 covers API-PTY-001 only. (d) The Address type change under the Party lock (API-PTY-013 versus API-PTY-011 or 015 on the same type).
findings.fix: Add four barrier TCs derived from AC-PTY-128, AC-PTY-129, AC-PTY-063 and AC-PTY-036. Each asserts the single end state and the loser's catalog code. Update N13, the Package table and COVERAGE.

findings.clause: "A copy of a core class, a `com.erp.*` package in the application, an edit to a core migration" (checklist F8)
findings.problem: The module root package is `com.erp.pty` (CORE module layout, manifest `package: com.erp.pty`, `com.erp.pty.crossmodule.PtyPartyApi`, `PtyPermissions`). `com.erp.*` is the core's namespace (core-manifest: com.erp.sec, com.erp.mdl, …). The library's own module example uses an application namespace (`package: com.acme.rental.leasing`). The same pattern appears in CAT v2 (`com.erp.cat`), so it is a rule-level defect.
findings.fix: Choose one application root namespace for all business modules, for example `com.<vendor>.commerce`. Record it once in the profile or domain profile and in an ADR. Rename PTY's package to `<root>.pty` (CORE layout, manifest, PtyPartyApi, Javadoc/README, test-plan references), and keep the boundary rule `<root>.pty.crossmodule`. File a platform finding so that CAT's next pass applies the same rename.

findings.clause: P2 closure — who may not read a record
findings.problem: API-PTY-002 serialises creditLimit, paymentTermDays and currencyCode to any holder of PERM_PTY_CUSTOMER_VIEW while the flag is on. A custom role without PERM_PTY_CUSTOMER_CREDIT_VIEW therefore reads credit data, which SCR-REQ-PTY-003 B4 gates. No requirement settles this either way.
findings.fix: Record in an ADR that Customer VIEW includes reading the credit values, because consumers rely on CON-PTY-009. This is the best-practice choice, since editing stays gated. Add an AC and a TC.

findings.problem: QR-PTY-011 uses the parameter `:tDigits`, but the query defines only `:t` and `:tAr`.
findings.fix: Define `:tDigits = '%'||REGEXP_REPLACE(term,'[ -]','','g')||'%'`, state the %/_ escaping for each form, and add an AC for a term containing spaces.

findings.problem: API-PTY-035 returns NOT_APPLICABLE before it loads the Customer. With the flag off, an unknown or inactive Customer gets 200, and no AC fixes this order.
findings.fix: State the order 'load the Customer (404) → RULE-PTY-005 → flag' and add an AC and a TC for the combination of flag off and an inactive Customer.

findings.problem: The plan states the lock order 'Party first, then the child row', but the role endpoints (API-PTY-003, 004, 005, 008, 009, 010) lock the role row first and the Party second.
findings.fix: State the order once in CORE as 'role row → Party → Address and requests', or reorder the role endpoints.

findings.problem: (1) The Customer picker of SCR-PTY-004 offers active Customers only and carries no isWalkInFl. The walk-in Customer is therefore offered and only refused after submit, and an inactive Customer's requests cannot be filtered from the picker. (2) The notification deep link has no upstream owner: the dispatch passes only referenceId and referenceType.
findings.fix: (1) Add isWalkInFl to `CustomerSearchHit` and have the picker hide the walk-in Customer. State that a customerId filter for an inactive Customer is reachable by URL only. (2) State the referenceType → route mapping in API-PTY-019 and F4, or drop the deep-link claim.

findings.problem: The test-plan headers cite REQ 109 · AC 123 · RULE 33 and a 36-row catalog; the current figures are 113, 136, 34 and 37. The frontend plan says 44 TCs in its header and 42 in its section text. The API-PTY-020 visibility rule (another user's request answers 404) has no TC.
findings.fix: Correct the counts. Add a backend TC: a requester without UPDATE reads another user's request → PTY-404-CREDIT-OVERRIDE-NOT-FOUND.

findings.problem: The manifest declares `api-paths: [/api/v1/pty]`. The library example uses a sub-tree pattern (`/api/v1/leasing/**`), so the bare prefix may match only the exact path.
findings.fix: Declare `api-paths: [/api/v1/pty/**]` in the manifest bullet of CORE.
